items.evidence: After a page.reload() the spec checks statusInfo is "Unfulfilled" and the fulfil button is visible (spec lines 87-91). It also first checks the order starts as "Fulfilled" with no fulfil button (lines 74-75), so these assertions would fail if the cancel mutation never ran.
All three criteria are asserted: the status is "Unfulfilled" (line 83), the fulfil action is offered again (line 84), and the order is still "Unfulfilled" after a reload (lines 88-90).

The cancel action is added to the existing OrderPage, reusing its dialog, timelineView, statusInfo and fulfillButton. The order is found with the existing findOrderId and ORDERS_SCENARIO. Nothing that already exists is copied.
No hard waits. The method waits on the dialog opening and closing (orderPage.ts lines 35 and 41).
test and expect come from fixtures/test.ts, the test is not tagged parallel(), and it does not write to the cache or the dumps.

All locators use test ids or roles, scoped to the card, the menu or the dialog. The submit button is this.dialog.getByTestId("submit"). .first() picks any warehouse, which the ticket allows; it is not used to find a specific element.
The spec uses the scenario's existing "fulfilled" order and does no set-up through the API or the UI.
No hard-coded ids. The order is looked up with findOrderId, and no populatedb warehouse names are asserted.
Uses the default admin actor's stored session and never signs in through the UI. The ticket names no permission.
The type check passes ("exit 0: no errors") and the spec is at e2e/tests/orders/order-cancel-fulfillment.spec.ts.
All locators and the multi-step action are on OrderPage. The spec only calls page-object members.
The new members are readonly fields built from this.page or this.dialog, and the existing constructor(readonly page: Page) {} is kept.
The spec has // Arrange and // Act & Assert comments (lines 68 and 77).
One test, with a test.step for each stage: cancel, check the result, reload.
The title says what behaviour is checked and carries #e2e.
A header comment (lines 58-62) says what the spec covers and why.
All assertions are web-first (toHaveText, toHaveCount, toBeVisible).
Uses ORDERS_SCENARIO and the "fulfilled" key from SCENARIO_ORDERS. The status strings are UI text, as in the sibling order specs. No money or arithmetic.
No cleanup code and no unique names.
No timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.
All relative imports keep .ts, and test and expect come only from the fixture.
No any, no casts, no gql calls.
The comments give reasons (portaled menu and listbox, Timeline-only card, pre-selected warehouse, why the preconditions matter) rather than restating the code.

structured_output.summary: Submission 1e0c7803 meets all 23 checklist items (B1–B10 and M1–M13). The spec opens the scenario's fulfilled order and first checks that it reads "Fulfilled" with no fulfil button. It then cancels the fulfillment through a new OrderPage.cancelFulfillment() method and checks that the order reads "Unfulfilled" with the fulfil button showing, both straight away and after a page reload. The reload check means the test would fail if the server never cancelled the fulfillment. Locators are test ids or roles, scoped to the card, menu or dialog, and the type check passes. One side note outside the checklist: the diff also adds a planning file, specs/order-cancel-fulfillment.md, which the ticket does not ask for.
